content:
Apple is expected to hold an event next week on October 13 to launch multiple new products. Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman said the product launch will take the form of an "event". Here's what he said.

Gurman said Apple will unveil three new products at its October 13 event

It's been almost a month since Apple's last event, which featured the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, among others.

However, reports indicate Apple's October event could be held as early as next Tuesday, October 13.

Gurman previously reported that these three products would launch on October 13, but at the time he did not mention they would be unveiled at a formal event.

There has been much debate over whether these new home products warrant a dedicated event. John Gruber, for example, has said the HomePad "absolutely cannot" be announced via a press release alone. He wrote: "If this product really launches, it has to be a keynote video paired with some kind of media event, with hands-on access."

And from Gurman's latest newsletter, he clearly agrees. "Apple is planning to hold an event on October 13," — that sounds pretty unequivocal.

If the event does happen, invitations are expected to go out to the media within the next day or two. Unless new CEO John Ternus plans to break with past practice and overhaul the way products are unveiled.

Do you think Apple's home devices will get a full October event, or just a press release? Let us know in the comments.
